biome_panoramas: Original production pixel-art landscape sheet for A Stroke of Luck, approved arcade landscape style. Four SEPARATE panoramas in exactly two columns and two rows, each 16:9. Total canvas 2048x1152; no gutters, no labels, no text, no borders or frames. Each scene has broad sky bands in upper half, large calm mid-distance silhouettes in lower half, dark foreground corner masses; central lower area quiet for an opaque top-down game board overlay. Deliberate crisp pixel clusters, stepped edges, selective fine details, no painterly realism, no blur or texture noise. Warm/cool palette hierarchy, 4 to 6 shade groups. Upper left DESERT: buttery warm light, pale apricot sky/cloud bands, distant desaturated terracotta mesas and buttes, sweeping ochre dunes, two asymmetric deep rust sandstone crags at lower corners, one silhouette cactus cluster far right. Upper right AUTUMN: honey sunset sky, layers of smoky teal distant hills contrasting burnt orange and sienna deciduous canopy masses, dark plum foreground trunks and irregular maple foliage on both lower corners; leaf silhouettes distinct from evergreen. Lower left SNOW: pale peach winter dawn sky, misty blue and mauve distant mountains, middle snowy ridges with crisp cool slate faces, dark blue spruce silhouettes framing the lower corners, broad lavender shadow snowfields; enough saturation and value contrast, not white everywhere. Lower right SWAMP: muted amber-green twilight opening in misty sky, three hazy moss-teal cypress forest bands, broad dark reflective wetland spaces and dense reeds at bottom edges, ancient crooked cypress trunk silhouette at left, dangling willow vine silhouette at right; organic wetland composition distinct from meadow, not spooky horror. Every scene individually composed, not six recolors or generic repetitive props. Absolutely no characters, balls, golf course, UI, signs, watermarks, fake screenshot. Original artistic work, not copied from a game.
biome_objects: Original practical pixel-art production atlas for A Stroke of Luck. TRUE TRANSPARENT PNG background, exactly 4 columns by2 rows, canvas1536x1024, each object centered in own384x512 cell with clear margins. No text, no labels, no grid, no panels, no floor squares, no cast shadows outside object. Hard pixel-art contours, controlled 4-6 tone ramps, selective dark outlines and cream upper-left highlights; individually illustrated game sprites, no painterly brushwork or 3D. Eight objects read left to right: TOP ROW: (1) a substantial branching desert saguaro cactus cluster with one smaller companion and a tiny pink bloom, sage/jade ridges, warm ochre foot rocks; (2) an irregular autumn maple tree with visible dark plum trunk, layered amber/copper maple-leaf silhouette clusters and a few fallen leaves at the base, not a sphere topiary; (3) an asymmetrical snow-covered spruce tree with broad crisp snow ledges and deep cold blue needles, rooted trunk, avoid white-on-white detail; (4) an ancient swamp cypress tree with roots, olive/jade drooping canopy and hanging moss, two reeds at base, distinct crooked silhouette. BOTTOM ROW: (1) full-square top-down falling ice block, frosty blue rim, translucent-looking flat ice face with three designed polygon facets and one jagged white crack, no perspective side projection, square silhouette fills its own inner square; (2) horizontal long narrow rotating lava hazard rod, dark forged bronze frame enclosing molten orange inset with gold hot core, central circular bearing, two capped ends, physical silhouette rectangular and uniform width; (3) a square inset brass-and-teal directional force mechanism viewed from above, with one broad pale right-pointing arrow inlay and four corner bolts, low mechanical floor plate, no outer ground; (4) small composed vegetation accent cluster of yellow daisies and pale mint reeds with clear planted bases, less than half the visual size of the trees. Sprite illustration logical resolution about72px for tree widths,48px for mechanism width except rod144px. True alpha including interior gaps. No ball, no tee, no UI button. Consistent original arcade world art.
